reviews.title: Buyer Beware! Poor Quality, Overpriced, and Disappointing
reviews.text:
I purchased Dressly expecting a quality personal styling experience with attractive, relevant outfit recommendations. What I got was an extremely disappointing selection of clothing that lacked style, variety, and any meaningful value.

The recommendations were so underwhelming that I canceled my subscription within MINUTES of opening and reviewing the app. That’s how quickly I realized I’d wasted my money.

But here’s where the experience gets even worse.

Despite explaining that I canceled almost immediately because of the poor quality of the selections, customer support initially responded by explaining how I had authorized the purchase rather than addressing my actual complaint.

After requesting a full refund, I was offered only 50% of my $59.99 payment. Apparently, even canceling within minutes after discovering how disappointing the service is isn’t enough to warrant a full refund.

My biggest complaint isn’t simply that I disliked the clothing. It’s that the quality of the recommendations was nowhere near what I expected from a paid styling service, and the response to my dissatisfaction was equally disappointing.

For $59.99, I expected thoughtful styling, appealing outfit combinations, and recommendations worth paying for. Dressly delivered none of that for me.

My advice? Don’t let the marketing convince you that you’re getting a premium personal styling experience. Look carefully at the subscription terms and refund policy before handing over your money.

I regret this purchase, I would not recommend this app, and I certainly won’t be returning.

One star because zero isn’t an option.

reviews.title: Ai outfits
reviews.text:
I’m on my first month of using AI Outfits, and I’ve found it helpful as a learning tool. I wish I could go back and read previous articles, but overall, it’s been useful. The app itself is a little sloppy and hasn’t been very responsive or helpful at times. The outfit try-on features are fun, but the app often distorts your features, and you can’t easily tell if the outfit will really fit you. And after a few tries, you don’t look like yourself anymore. After waiting a week for a capsule to be generated, it didn’t generate one with the colors that were recommended for my skin. and you can’t seem to ask for it to make a new capsule. 

My least favorite part is that the app doesn’t let you sync between my iPhone and iPad. I even took a lot of photos of my wardrobe to add to the app from my iPhone, but they don’t show up when I use the iPad. I like to use both devices, especially since I can see things better on the iPad.

reviews.text:
I signed up expecting to use the app right away, but I had to wait days before I could fully use its features. That was frustrating, so I decided to cancel on day three.

I went through the cancellation process in the app on October 8. When I was charged the $49.99 renewal fee on October 31, I canceled again and emailed Dressly. I even sent them a screenshot showing me going through the cancellation process on October 8. Despite that proof, they refused to refund the charge or do anything to resolve the issue.

I had to spend time emailing support just to cancel, and my screenshot was not enough to get the charge addressed. The app should make its features usable without a long wait, and cancellation should be clear and reliable. Based on my experience, I can’t recommend it.

In April, I spent $15.19 with Dressly. Cute! Fun! A little treat!

What I did not realize was that Dressly and I had apparently entered into a committed relationship, because every four weeks thereafter they came back for $49.99.

May: $49.99
June: $49.99
July: $49.99
August: $49.99

Meanwhile, I’m just out here living my life, completely unaware. I finally noticed the charge today, logged into my account (that I didn’t know I had), and discovered I’ve paid an additional $199.96 for a subscription I didn’t realize I had. Obviously, I’ve now canceled it and requested my money back.

Maybe the recurring subscription was disclosed somewhere during my original purchase, but it certainly wasn’t clear enough for me to realize I was signing up to donate $49.99 to the Dressly Foundation every 28 days. It isn’t even under my “subscriptions” or anything in my iphone. 

So, friends, if you’ve ever bought something from Dressly, go check your bank statement. 

Be careful out there. 😂

reviews.title: Warning: The $19.99 is a scam
reviews.text:
The app has potential — it's visually appealing and a decent starting point if you're into personal image. But, they offer what they call a "personalized consultation" for $19.99. What you actually get is a generic PDF that anyone could generate in minutes using free AI tools. Nothing personalized about it.

The "daily outfits" feature is just as generic — think Instagram store ads. You end up picking whatever catches your eye anyway, which defeats the purpose. The concept is good, but it still needs a lot of work.

To make it worse, since it's delivered by email, they refuse to issue any refund. So once you pay, you're stuck.

Save your money. The app itself is okay to browse for free, but do NOT fall for the upsell. It's misleading at best, a scam at worst.

Also, REMEMBER TO CANCEL because it’s $99 when it AUTO renewed. I thought well maybe there will be more tutorials but NO. ALL you get for the $99 is the ability to try on outfits. TOTAL RIP OFF. Especially when it isn’t using my original picture of ME!  I don’t care what a “model” looks like.  I’m 5’1” tall. Not 5’11.
